notes: Phase 2 M1 source pack for Nigeria Evidence Hardening I / I-B. Scope limited to NG-B1 outbound foreign-currency cash mechanics, NG-B6 declaration threshold, and NG-B7 physical naira import/export rule. Hardening I-B (2026-09-09): (1) no later primary instrument was found reconciling MLPPA 2022 'in excess of' with NCS e-CDF 'or more'/'equal to or greater than', so dual operators are preserved rather than force-reconciled; (2) bounded primary search did not pin a current CBN-hosted guideline/FX Manual PDF establishing a live numeric traveller exception under FEMMPA s.14, so numeric exception = not established. Secondary press/law-firm references to N100,000 remain discovery-only and are not adopted.

sources.authority: Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment
sources.notes: Used here for section 14 naira import/export prohibition and section 21 domiciliary-account cash mechanics. Section 12's US$5,000 declaration wording is retained only for temporal audit because later AML legislation uses US$10,000.

sources.label: Nigeria Customs Service — Electronic Currency Declaration
sources.notes: Operational current guidance and e-form. Uses '$10,000 or more' / 'equal to or greater than' wording. Hardening I-B preserves this as the operational operator (>=) alongside the statutory MLPPA operator (>); no reconciling primary instrument was pinned.

source_conflicts.detail: Money Laundering Act section 3(3) uses 'in excess of US$10,000' (operator >) while the current Nigeria Customs e-declaration form uses '$10,000 or more' / 'equal to or greater than $10,000' (operator >=). Hardening I-B bounded search found no later primary amending or interpretive instrument that formally reconciles the operators. Customs press language often restates 'exceeding', but the live e-form remains inclusive. Disposition: preserve dual operators; do not flatten > into >= or vice versa.
source_conflicts.wording_boundary: Statutory declaration trigger remains 'in excess of US$10,000'. Operational Customs e-form trigger remains 'US$10,000 or more'. Future wording must keep both roles distinct and must not invent a single reconciled operator.

missing_authorities.topic: current guideline exception under section 14 of the Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act for physical naira import/export
missing_authorities.reason: Hardening I-B bounded primary search (CBN-hosted FX Manual PDF; current Monetary/Credit/Foreign Trade guidelines PDF; CBN circulars expressly implementing FEMMPA s.14 traveller exceptions) did not pin a currently operative official instrument establishing a live numeric traveller exception threshold for physical naira notes. Historical CBN guideline language (for example older N10,000 declaration wording) and secondary press/law-firm summaries referring to N100,000 were treated as discovery aids only and were not adopted. Conclusion: numeric exception = not established.
missing_authorities.wording_boundary: Publish only the FEMMPA s.14 prohibition baseline plus the fact that any numeric traveller exception remains not established. Do not invent N10,000, N20,000, N100,000, or any other numeric NGN carriage/exception figure from secondary sources.
